# National University of Singapore (NUS): Prestige, Structure, and Legacy
Celebrating its 120th anniversary since evolving from a 1905 medical school through mergers with Raffles College and Nanyang University, NUS is a globally prestigious institution renowned for its high internationality (65% foreign nationals) and top-tier rankings, consistently holding the #1 national position and frequently ranking in the global top 30. Its academic portfolio spans multiple campuses, including Kent Ridge, Bukit Timah, and the 2011-opened NUS University Town (UTown)—a former golf course now housing colleges, research institutes, and specialized residential colleges. The university features a modular structure of 17 faculties reorganized into interdisciplinary colleges (Design and Engineering, Humanities and Sciences, and Integrative Sciences and Engineering) and offers extensive programs in Law, Medicine, Public Health, and more.

# National University of Singapore (NUS): Prestige, Structure, and Legacy
## Resources, Research, and Administration
NUS supports innovation through 21 research institutes focused on biomedical science, engineering, and nanoscience, alongside entrepreneurship initiatives. Extensive resources include NUSNET, the Digital Gems archive (containing historical documents, maps, and private papers of figures like Carl A. Trocki), and specialized libraries. Leadership has been guided by a succession of presidents from 1905 to the present, with Tan Eng Chye currently serving as the leader. Notable recent structural changes include the dissolution of Yale-NUS College in 2025, which merged into NUS College, integrating the University Scholars Programme.

# National University of Singapore (NUS): Prestige, Structure, and Legacy
## Legacy and Impact
NUS graduates are recognized as among the most employable worldwide, and its coat of arms, adopted in 1980, symbolizes Singapore's lion, knowledge, and creativity. The institution boasts a distinguished alumni network comprising two Singaporean prime ministers (Lee Kuan Yew, Goh Chok Tong), four presidents (including Tony Tan and S. R. Nathan), multiple Malaysian prime ministers (including Mahathir Mohamad), and prominent leaders in business, politics, and international organizations (including Margaret Chan as WHO Director-General). Historically serving as Singapore's sole law school until 2007, NUS has educated numerous influential judges and ministers, such as K. Shanmugam, Chan Sek Keong, and Sundaresh Menon, alongside key historians like Wang Gungwu.
